markets.question: Superhuman Coder (SC) milestone — AI that can do any coding task the best AGI-company engineer does, faster and cheaper. When does it arrive?
markets.forecast: All-things-considered median 2028-2030; 2027 is among the single most likely years. Eli Lifland: time-horizon model Feb 2029 (80% CI Apr 2026-2052), benchmarks-and-gaps Mar 2030. Nikola Jurkovic: 2027-2028. Original AI 2027 headline median ~Mar 2027; updated forecasts pushed later. Non-trivial probability mass on end-2026/2027 but it is not the median.

markets.question: METR task-completion time horizon (length of software task a frontier model can do at 50% reliability) — where does it land?
markets.forecast: Frontier as of Jan 2026: Claude Opus 4.5 ~320 min (~5.3 hr), GPT-5 ~214 min, o3 ~121 min. Doubling time ~89-131 days (≈3-4.3 months) on the 2024+ trend (~10x/yr at the fast rate). Extrapolation puts frontier near ~600+ min by end-2026 and month-long tasks plausibly in 2027 if the fast trend holds; debate on whether it reverts to the 7-month doubling.

markets.question: SWE-bench Verified — best frontier score
markets.platform: Stanford AI Index 2026 / Epoch AI / live leaderboards
markets.forecast: Effectively saturated. Rose from ~60% to near-100% in one year (Stanford AI Index 2026). Current top (Jun 18 2026): Claude Mythos 5 95.5%, Claude Fable 5 95%, Claude Opus 4.8 88.6%. Forecast: ceiling ~95-99% reached during 2026; benchmark loses discriminating power, focus shifting to agentic/long-horizon variants.

markets.question: GPQA Diamond (PhD-level science) — best frontier score
markets.platform: Metaculus / Epoch AI / Stanford AI Index 2026
markets.forecast: Metaculus forecasters: 97.3% in 2026, 98.9% in 2027 (30% chance of ≥99%). Current: Gemini 3.1 Pro 94.1%, Grok 4 87%; models already past the 81.2% human-expert baseline (hitting ~93%). Near-saturated.

markets.question: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — frontier ceiling and trajectory
markets.forecast: Index repeatedly rebased as it saturates: v3 top models tied ~57 (Apr 2026); a June public snapshot shows Claude Opus 4.8 ~55.7, GPT-5.5 ~54.8. AA dropped MMLU-Pro/AIME-2025/LiveCodeBench in v4 (Jan 2026) due to saturation. No single AA point-forecast exists; trajectory = steady rise into the high-50s/60s on current scale, with the index re-versioned rather than left to cap out. Humanity's Last Exam (a component) still only ~35-45%, the main remaining headroom.

markets.question: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) — frontier score (the hardest unsaturated component of AA Index)
markets.forecast: Frontier gained ~30 percentage points in one year. Current leaders ~35-45% (Gemini 3.1 Pro 44.7%); human experts ~90%, leaving a 45-55 pt gap. This is the benchmark with real headroom into 2027; rapid gains expected but full saturation unlikely by end-2026.

markets.question: Frontier training compute — when does the top model trend cross 1e26 FLOP, and how fast does it grow?
markets.forecast: Training compute growing ~4-5x/year (doubling ~5.2 months) since 2020. Top-1 frontier crosses 1e26 FLOP median ~Jan 2026; frontier open-weight models cross 1e26 ~Nov 2025 (90% CI to Nov 2026). Largest known run: Grok 4 ~5e26 FLOP. Extrapolation: largest runs ~1e27-1e28 FLOP by end-2027, ~1e29 by 2030.

markets.question: How many notable AI models will exceed 1e26 FLOP of training compute?
markets.forecast: ~10 models by 2026, between 10 and 80 by 2027, ~80 by 2028, 200+ by 2030.

markets.question: Pace of frontier model releases in 2026
markets.forecast: Most compressed release cycle on record: ~7 frontier models Feb-Apr 2026 alone. ~5 major closed releases since Feb (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.3) plus 6+ major open-weight (DeepSeek V4, Qwen3-Coder-Next, GLM-5, Kimi K2.6, etc.). Each major lab shipping a new flagship roughly every 1-3 months; no slowdown projected. Polymarket: 'best AI model end of June' ~95% Anthropic.

markets.question: AI vs human forecasting (Metaculus FutureEval) — when do AI systems surpass humans at prediction?
markets.forecast: AI projected to surpass the broader Metaculus community ~Apr 2026 and Pro Forecasters ~mid-2027.

markets.question: AGI timeline (prediction-market / aggregate forecaster view)
markets.forecast: ~25% chance of AGI by 2029, 50% by 2033. Contrast: Grace et al. expert survey median for High-Level Machine Intelligence ~2047 (shortened 13 yrs vs the 2022 survey). Markets far more aggressive than the academic survey median.

result.methodology: These forecasts are anchored to live prediction markets and expert projections, not freehand guesses: release timing comes from Polymarket's dated release markets (GPT-5.6 ~96% by Jul 31; GPT-6 52% by Sep / 82% by Dec; Gemini 4.0 only ~10% by Jun 30; the $4.49M Claude 5 market pricing no Claude 5 before Q3) and the industry "best model" markets (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold pricing Anthropic ~64% to hold #1 at year-end, Google ~13-15% and OpenAI ~10-12% as the leading challengers). Benchmark ceilings are pinned to Epoch AI / Stanford AI Index 2026 (SWE-bench Verified effectively saturating at ~95-96% with frontier-accessible models around 88-95%) and the Artificial Analysis Index trajectory (frontier in the high-50s/low-60s on current v3/v4 scale, rising steadily but re-versioned as it saturates), then each lab's own AA/SWE back-trajectory from the historical backfill sets the slope and the gap-to-frontier. Where a market is silent on a specific lab (Zhipu, Alibaba, Meta), I extrapolate that lab's documented release cadence (~1-3 months per flagship, per the LM Council / release-pace tracker) and its current distance behind the leader, widening the uncertainty bands to reflect the thinner evidence.

verify.fact: GPT-4 scored only about 1.7% on the original SWE-bench when it was introduced in 2023.
verify.note: CONFIRMED by the primary source: the original SWE-bench paper (Jimenez et al., "SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?", arXiv:2310.06770, first posted Oct 2023, later ICLR 2024). Extracted the PDF text directly (saved at /Users/christian/.claude/projects/-Users-christian/376db47d-cee0-426f-9ede-41c2b74b4921/tool-results/webfetch-1781902154849-yk3u6u.pdf). In Table 18 ("Oracle" Retrieval, the main per-model retrieval setting), GPT-4 (model gpt-4-32k-0613) resolved exactly 1.74% (34.00% apply rate) — this matches "about 1.7%." Two honesty caveats that do not break the claim: (1) GPT-4's score depended on retrieval setting: 1.3% with BM25, 1.74% with "Oracle," and 3.40% with the more generous "Oracle-collapsed" setting — so "1.7%" is the standard oracle number, not a single universal figure. (2) Per the paper's footnote, GPT-4 was evaluated only on a 25% random subset of SWE-bench tasks due to budget constraints, not the full test set. Also note a common confusion: the paper's frequently-quoted headline "best model resolves only 1.96%" refers to Claude 2 (BM25), not GPT-4. But the specific claim about GPT-4 ~1.7% is accurate against the original 2023 benchmark.

verify.fact: The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index did not exist before roughly 2024.
verify.note:
Confirmed against primary and secondary sources. Artificial Analysis (the independent AI-benchmarking site at artificialanalysis.ai) was founded in 2023 (per its company profile / Grokipedia and PitchBook listings). Its Intelligence Index version history, on the company's own methodology page (https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking), dates v1.0 to January 2024, with v1.0–1.3 spanning Jan 2024–Feb 2025, then v2.x (2025), v3.0 (Sep 2025), v4.0 (Jan 2026), and v4.1 (Jun 2026). Since the company itself only launched in 2023 and the index's first version is dated January 2024, no such index existed before ~2024 — the claim holds.

Two caveats: (1) Do NOT confuse this with the Stanford HAI "AI Index Report," a separate, distinct publication running annually since 2017 — that one DID exist before 2024, but it is not the "Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index." (2) The decisive Jan-2024/v1.0 date came from a WebFetch read of the methodology page; I could not independently re-surface that exact string in search snippets, but the corroborated 2023 founding date makes any pre-2024 Intelligence Index impossible regardless. Verdict: confirmed; "roughly 2024" is accurate (v1.0 = Jan 2024).

verify.fact: OpenAI o1 substantially raised frontier scores on reasoning/coding benchmarks vs GPT-4o in late 2024.
verify.note: CONFIRMED via OpenAI's official "Learning to reason with LLMs" announcement (Sept 12, 2024), corroborated across multiple independent sources (Vellum, Analytics Vidhya, Encord, TalkAI). The gains are large and not marginal: AIME 2024 math — GPT-4o ~12-13% vs o1 74% single-sample / 83% with consensus sampling (a ~6x jump). Codeforces competitive coding — GPT-4o 808 Elo (~11th percentile) vs o1 89th percentile. GPQA Diamond PhD-science — o1 exceeded GPT-4o and surpassed human PhD-level accuracy. MMLU — o1 beat GPT-4o on 54 of 57 subcategories. The "frontier" framing is accurate: these were SOTA reasoning results at release. One precision caveat worth flagging — the headline 83%/89th-percentile figures are for the full o1 model; the model actually released to the public in Sept 2024 was o1-preview, which scored somewhat lower (e.g. ~62nd-percentile Codeforces, lower AIME) but still well above GPT-4o. So the directional claim is solid regardless of which o1 variant you anchor on; only the exact magnitude shifts. Sources: https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/ ; https://www.vellum.ai/blog/analysis-openai-o1-vs-gpt-4o ; https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/2024/09/gpt-4o-vs-openai-o1/

verify.fact: DeepSeek R1 (Jan 2025) brought open-weights reasoning close to the proprietary frontier.
verify.note: Confirmed against primary sources. DeepSeek's own arXiv paper (2501.12948v1) abstract states verbatim: "DeepSeek-R1 achieves performance comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217 on reasoning tasks." Released Jan 20, 2025 under MIT license with fully open weights (R1, R1-Zero, plus six distilled 1.5B-70B checkpoints) per DeepSeek's official release notes ("Performance on par with OpenAI-o1"; "released under the MIT License"). Benchmark numbers show near-parity with OpenAI's then-frontier reasoning model o1-1217: AIME 2024 79.8% (R1) vs 79.2% (o1), MATH-500 97.3% vs 96.4%; o1 held a slight edge on GPQA Diamond and Codeforces. Additionally peer-reviewed in Nature (2025, s41586-025-09422-z) — unusually strong validation for an LLM release. One minor framing note: the apt frontier comparison is o1, not o3 (announced but not broadly released in Jan 2025); the claim's hedge "close to the frontier" accommodates this and does not overreach. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948, api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250120, nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09422-z.
